To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Wee1 inhibitor combined with histone de-acetylase inhibitors synergistically kills acute myeloid leukaemia cells and primitive progenitors in vitro and in vivo.

a combination regimen of Wee1 inhibitor (AZD1775) and histone deacetylation inhibitor (HDACi, for example, vorinostat) synergistically kills human AML cells harboring various mutations, including FLT3-ITDs, and primitive leukemia-initiating progenitor populations, in association with pronounced inhibition of Wee1 and Chk1 and diminished cdc/Cdk1 Y-15 phosphorylation, and is active in AML murines xenografts

a regimen combining the Weel inhibitor AZD177 with histone deacytlase inhibitors potently targets human acute myeoloid leukemia cells, and is particularly active against cells bearing poor prognosis genetic aberrations, such as FLT3-internal tandem duplication and p53 mutations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new treatment strategy for patients with acute myelogenous leukemias.
the use of Wee1 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for the treatment of acute myeloid leukemias (AMLs) with poor prognostics.
the development of novel therapies for AML.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of Wee1 inhibitor with HDACI is an effective therapeutic strategy in AML.
the combination of AZD1775 (Wee1 inhibitor) and Vorinostat (HDACI) targets human acute myleoid leukemia cells harbored various genetic mutations.
the Wee1 and HDAC inhibitors synergize in AML cells and this combination warrants further investigation in the treatment of AML.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AZD1776 and HDACI combination treatment is an effective strategy against human AML, including AML with FLT3-ITDs and p53 mutations.
Wee1 inhibition in combination with HDACI can be used to kill leukemia cells harboring different genetic mutations.
Wee1 inhibition in combination with HDAC inhibitors is an effective therapeutic strategy for AML, particularly for those with poor prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of AZD1775, a Wee1 inhibitor, and a histone deacetylation inhibitor (HDACI) is synergistic in killing acute myeloid leukemic cells, and this combination is active against leukemic cells with poor prognostics such as p53 mutations.

the combination of Wee1 inhibition with histone deactylase inhibitors is a highly effective regimen against acute myelogenous leukemias with various next-generation sequencing defined mutations and that this regimen has the potential for clinical development.

the Wee1 kinase inhibitor AZD1777 synergizes with HDAC inhibitors to kill AML cells, including those harboring p53 mutations, through p53-dependent and -independent mechanisms, and this combination is effective against AML-initiating cells.
